# T7.00: why a third party cannot register a VideoToolbox encoder system-wide (and how CLI tools get ours anyway)

Goal: make our NVENC encoder available to every app that uses VideoToolbox, including command-line tools (ffmpeg,
HandBrakeCLI, avconvert), the way Apple's own encoders are. Finding (macOS 26.7.1, 2026-10-18): **macOS has no supported
way for a third party to register a video *encoder* system-wide.** Apple provides one for decoders and deliberately not
for encoders. GUI apps still get ours in-process (the Metal plugin); CLI tools need injection (`nvenc-run`). This report
records why, so we do not re-investigate it.

## The three registration mechanisms, and which wall each hits

VideoToolbox finds an encoder for `VTCompressionSessionCreate` in its encoder registry (a CoreMedia `FigRegistry` of
class `com.apple.videotoolbox.videoencoder`). Three ways to get into it:

1. **In-process `VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo`.** Works, but only in the calling process, and only while it runs. This
   is what the Metal plugin does: it loads `libnvencvt.dylib` when a process creates a Metal device, and the encoder
   registers itself. Covers GUI apps (Parsec, OBS, AVFoundation apps) that use the GPU. Shipped since v2.3.6-mickys.2;
   names fixed in .8 (see `T7.00-names.md`). Does **not** cover a process that never creates a Metal device.

2. **A plug-in bundle in a scanned folder — blocked by Apple code-signing.** VideoToolbox scans
   `/System/Library/Video/Plug-Ins`, `/Library/Video/Plug-Ins` and two `/AppleInternal` folders, and *does* find and
   cache a third-party bundle placed in `/Library/Video/Plug-Ins`. But it adds every search path with an option bit that
   makes CoreMedia's `figRegistryAddResultItem` check each bundle against `kFigRegistryAppleCodeSignRequirement`:
   `anchor apple or anchor apple generic and info[CFBundleIdentifier] = "com.apple."* and certificate leaf[1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.9 or .27]`.
   Only Apple can satisfy it (a Developer ID cert carries extension .13, not .9/.27). Our ad-hoc-signed probe is scanned,
   cached, and then dropped from the result list. `VTRegisterVideoEncoderBundleDirectory(CFURL)` is no help: it only
   accepts a folder under `/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/` or inside a bundle signed like the app's own main bundle.
   The relaxed AMFI/SIP boot settings this driver needs do **not** change this: the signature check is a user-space
   `Security.framework` call about *who signed the bundle*, not kernel code-signing enforcement. Details and the
   disassembly: `T7.00-names.md` step 2.

3. **A MediaExtension extension — exists for decoders, not for encoders.** MediaExtension.framework (macOS 15+, present
   on 26) is Apple's modern, out-of-process, sandboxed codec-plugin mechanism, meant to replace the legacy in-process
   registration. On the guest its extension points are **formatreader, videodecoder, rawprocessor only** (framework
   `Info.plist`; SDK headers are `MEFormatReader.h`, `MEVideoDecoder.h`, `MERAWProcessor.h`). There is no `MEVideoEncoder`,
   no encoder extension point, and no "encoder" string in the framework binary. So the clean, Apple-blessed path covers
   decode and not encode.

## "Just register as a decoder" does not work

Three independent reasons, from Apple's own `MEVideoDecoder.h`:
- **Wrong pipe.** "MediaExtension video decoder operation and life cycle are closely tied to VTDecompressionSession …
  These calls correspond to VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrame calls on the parent VTDecompressionSession." The only
  frame callback is `decodeFrameFromSampleBuffer:` (compressed in, pixels out). An app that *encodes* calls
  `VTCompressionSessionCreate`, which reads the *encoder* registry (class `…videoencoder`); a decoder lives in the
  *decoder* registry (class `…videodecoder`), a different object the encode path never iterates. A decoder is structurally
  never invoked on the encode path, whatever we label it.
- **Out of process.** It is an ExtensionKit `.appex` (connection handler `MEVideoDecoderConnectionHandler`) in its own
  sandbox, so our code is not even in the encoding app's process to do any in-process trick.
- **Entitlement-gated.** The header requires the entitlement `com.apple.developer.mediaextension.videodecoder` with a
  provisioning profile — Apple signing again.

## Not a counter-example: the OBS "customizable encoders" plugin

`Neotecos/obs-macos-videotoolbox-encoders` looks like a third party adding VT encoders, but its `src/encoder.c` only
calls `obs_register_encoder` (an OBS plugin) and wraps Apple's *existing* VT encoders: it enumerates them by
`kVTVideoEncoderList_EncoderID` and opens a `VTCompressionSession` on them, exposing OBS settings. It registers nothing
with VideoToolbox.

## What we ship instead

- **GUI apps:** mechanism 1 (the Metal plugin), done.
- **CLI tools:** injection. `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=…/libnvencvt.dylib <tool>` loads our encoder into the tool's process,
  where it self-registers. Measured on the guest (this driver's boot settings `amfi_get_out_of_my_way=0x1`, relaxed SIP):
  it reaches unsigned binaries (evermeet/Homebrew ffmpeg), a hardened-runtime test binary (`flags=runtime`), and Apple's
  SIP-protected `/usr/bin/avconvert`. On a stock Mac the hardened runtime would strip `DYLD_*`, but a stock Mac cannot run
  this driver. Planned as `nvenc-run` in the overlay (see notes/TODO.md item 0). This is the real replacement for the
  blocked bundle route; it does not give system-wide auto-loading, which only a bundle (mechanism 2) could.

## For the user to consider

A Feedback request to Apple is the legitimate ask, and it is now concrete: MediaExtension has a video *decoder* extension
point (`com.apple.mediaextension.videodecoder`, `MEVideoDecoder`) but no *encoder* counterpart; request an `MEVideoEncoder`
so third-party hardware encoders can register out-of-process like decoders do. User's to file.

## What NOT to do

Patching CoreMedia to skip the signature check, or forcing the library into every process system-wide, means modifying the
signed system shared cache or a global `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`. The injection wrapper reaches every tool we tested without it.

**Update (2026-10-19):** the "patch CoreMedia" route was deliberately revisited and investigated end to end — see
[`T7.03-coremedia-codesign-investigation.md`](T7.03-coremedia-codesign-investigation.md) (summary:
[`T7.03-coremedia-codesign-summary.md`](T7.03-coremedia-codesign-summary.md)). The CoreMedia check was fully reversed and
reduced to exact patch candidates, but **an in-place patch of the dyld shared cache is infeasible on 25G241**: the kernel
re-validates cache pages by hash at page-in (not relaxed by `amfi_get_out_of_my_way`/`amfi`, and unrelated to the
authenticated-root/system-volume seal), so any edit SIGKILLs signed processes as they fault and panics the machine
(`CS_KILLED initproc`), confirmed both at boot and live with no reboot. So the system-wide bundle route stays closed below
user space; **do not patch the cache**. The injection wrapper (`nvenc-run`) and an Apple Feedback request for a MediaExtension
`MEVideoEncoder` extension point remain the routes.
